parole.significato: narrows, usually referring to a narrow mountain pass
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish دربند (derbent, dervent, “narrows, pass; derbend”) through Greek δερβένι (dervéni, “narrows, pass”), ultimately from Classical Persian دربند (darband, “narrows, pass”). The alternative form дервент (dervent) is attested later, and was formed from дервен (derven) under the influe
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قامبور (whence modern Turkish kambur), of Greek origin.

parole.significato: box, case (container with a flat base and sides)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قوطی (kutu, kutı) (extended with the suffix -ия (-ija)), ultimately from Greek κουτί (koutí).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish لوفر (lüfer), from Greek λουφάρι (loufári). Compare Turkish lüfer and Russian луфарь (lufarʹ).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مشمله (muşmula), from Greek μούσμουλο (moúsmoulo).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خمسی (hamsı), from Greek χαμψί (champsí). Cognates include Turkish hamsi, Romanian hamsie, Russian хамса (xamsa) and Kazakh қамса (qamsa).
